reading.title: The Pen in the Lost-and-Found
reading.intro_zh: 这篇短文不复述原文，而是换到一个校园失物的故事：丢的东西看起来糟糕，结果没那么坏，而且有人很诚实——回收 upset / sympathetic / complain / envelope / contained / honesty / It could be worse。
passage: On Friday, Leo could not find his pencil case after the school trip. It was only a cheap case, but it contained his grandmother's old fountain pen. He felt very upset and began to complain that someone must have taken it. The teacher was sympathetic, but she could do nothing until Monday. All weekend Leo imagined the worst. On Monday, a younger student came to the lost-and-found desk with a small envelope. Inside was the pen, safe and clean. "I saw it under a seat on the bus," she said. Leo smiled. "It could be worse," he told his teacher. "There is still some honesty in this world."

questions.question: What did Leo lose after the school trip?
options: His school bag.
His pencil case.
His bus ticket.
His teacher's envelope.
questions.explanation_zh: 第一句说明 Leo could not find his pencil case after the school trip。

questions.question: Why did losing the pencil case matter so much?
options: Because it contained his grandmother's old fountain pen.
Because it contained all the class money.
Because it was a very expensive case.
Because it belonged to a younger student.
questions.explanation_zh: 短文说铅笔盒本身不贵，但里面有祖母的旧钢笔。

questions.question: What could the teacher do at first?
options: She found the pen under the seat at once.
She asked every student to stay after school.
She bought Leo a new fountain pen.
She was sympathetic but could do nothing until Monday.
questions.explanation_zh: 短文写道：The teacher was sympathetic, but she could do nothing until Monday。

questions.question: Who returned the pen, and where?
options: A teacher returned it in the classroom.
A bus driver returned it at the station.
A younger student returned it at the lost-and-found desk.
Leo's grandmother returned it at home.
questions.explanation_zh: 周一，一个 younger student 把装着钢笔的小信封带到 lost-and-found desk。

questions.question: What does the ending show?
options: School trips always make students lose things.
The situation was not as bad as feared, and someone was honest.
Teachers should never wait until Monday.
Cheap pencil cases are not worth keeping.
questions.explanation_zh: Leo 原本 imagined the worst，但钢笔被诚实归还，所以结尾强调 It could be worse 和 honesty。

writing.intro_zh: 今天不做泛泛的造句，只抓四个值得背下来的结构：刚刚发生的事、同情但无能为力、动作被打断、以及有文采的收束句。

patterns.title: had just done + felt ...
patterns.source: I had just lost $50 and I felt very upset.
patterns.focus_zh: 用过去完成时说明“刚刚发生了一件事”，再接情绪。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：你刚丢了学生卡、钥匙或作业，所以很着急。
patterns.sample: I had just lost my student card and I felt very worried.
patterns.tip_zh: 这个结构比 I lost... 更有故事感：先交代刚刚发生的事，再说情绪。

patterns.title: was sympathetic, but ... could do nothing
patterns.source: The manager was sympathetic, but he could do nothing.
patterns.focus_zh: 这是很地道的转折：对方理解你，但客观上帮不上忙。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：老师、工作人员或同学理解你，但当时也帮不上忙。
patterns.sample: The teacher was sympathetic, but she could do nothing at that moment.
patterns.tip_zh: sympathetic 不是简单的 nice，而是“理解你的处境、同情你”。

patterns.title: started to complain about ... but was interrupted by ...
patterns.source: He started to complain about this wicked world but was interrupted by a knock at the door.
patterns.focus_zh: 连续动作有电影感：刚开始抱怨，就被一个声音或动作打断。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：某人开始抱怨噪音、天气或作业，却被电话、敲门或老师打断。
patterns.sample: He started to complain about the noise but was interrupted by a phone call.
patterns.tip_zh: 这个句式适合写故事转折，比 He complained. Then someone called. 更紧凑。

patterns.title: There is still some ... in this world.
patterns.source: There is still some honesty in this world!
patterns.focus_zh: 这是一个有文采的结尾句，用来表达“事情没有那么糟”。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：看到有人归还东西后，说世界上仍然有善意、诚实或希望。
patterns.sample: There is still some kindness in this world.
patterns.tip_zh: 这个句式可以把一个小故事收束成一句有力量的话。
